findings.explanation: The `update_subscription` PATCH endpoint (line 83) accepts a caller-supplied `email` query parameter and uses it directly to look up and modify a Stripe customer's subscriptions. Although the `@requires(['authenticated'])` decorator (line 82) ensures the caller is logged in, there is no check that the supplied `email` matches the authenticated user's own identity (`request.user.username`, which is set to the logged-in user's email by `AuthenticatedKhojUser.__init__` at configure.py:41). Any authenticated user can therefore cancel or resubscribe the Stripe subscription of any other user simply by supplying a different email address in the request — a classic IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference). The `UserAuthenticationBackend.authenticate` method (configure.py:63-81) populates `request.user` with the real user object, making the fix straightforward: compare `email` against `request.user.username` before proceeding.

evidence.content: Anonymous mode bypasses authentication for local, single-user usage — implying that in non-anonymous (multi-user) mode, operations must be scoped to the authenticated user, not to an arbitrary caller-supplied identifier.

findings.suggested_fix: After the `@requires(['authenticated'])` guard passes, verify that the caller-supplied `email` matches the authenticated user's own email before performing any Stripe operation. For example, add at the top of the function body: `if email != request.user.username: raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail='Forbidden')`. This ensures a user can only manage their own subscription.

findings.explanation: In `map_config_to_object`, line 67 duplicates the condition `content_source == DbEntry.EntrySource.GITHUB` instead of checking `DbEntry.EntrySource.NOTION`. This means the NOTION branch is dead code and will never be reached. As a result, when `remove_content_source_data` is called with a NOTION content_source, `map_config_to_object` returns `None` (falls through all branches without a return), causing a `ValueError` to be raised at line 242–243 before `EntryAdapters.delete_all_entries` is called. However, because the NotionConfig ORM record is never deleted (the `content_object.objects.filter(user=user).adelete()` at line 245 is never reached for NOTION), the authorization enforcement is incorrect: NOTION configuration data is silently preserved instead of being deleted, meaning the deletion operation does not correctly enforce the intended access-control outcome (deleting only the requesting user's NOTION config). Additionally, an authenticated user supplying `content_source=notion` will receive a `ValueError` instead of a successful delete, while their NotionConfig persists in the database.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the duplicate condition on line 67: change `if content_source == DbEntry.EntrySource.GITHUB:` to `if content_source == DbEntry.EntrySource.NOTION:` so that the NOTION branch correctly returns `NotionConfig` and the delete endpoint can properly remove the authenticated user's Notion configuration.

findings.explanation: In `remove_content_source_data`, the user-supplied `content_source` path parameter is passed directly as the `file_source` argument to `EntryAdapters.delete_all_entries` (line 246). The new `delete_all_entries` method (introduced in this PR) deletes all entries matching `file_source=content_source`. However, when `content_source` does not match any valid `EntrySource` choice (i.e., `map_config_to_object` returns `"Computer"` for the COMPUTER source, meaning the `content_object != "Computer"` branch is skipped), the arbitrary string is still passed to the DB filter. More critically, the new `delete_all_entries` method has a default of `file_source=None` which deletes ALL entries for the user when called with `None`. While the router always passes `content_source`, there is no validation that `content_source` is a valid `EntrySource` value before passing it to the deletion adapter — any authenticated user can supply an arbitrary string. This is an incorrect authorization check: the content_source value is accepted from the URL path without being validated against the `EntrySource` enum before being used to scope deletion, meaning a carefully crafted value that does not match any source silently deletes nothing, but the broader issue is that `map_config_to_object` returning `None` raises a `ValueError` before the deletion, yet the validation logic is inconsistent with the new `file_source` field's enum values (e.g., `"computer"` vs `"Computer"`). A user supplying `content_source="computer"` (lowercase) would pass the `map_config_to_object` check (which likely maps to `"Computer"`) but delete entries tagged `file_source="computer"` — effectively bypassing the intended scoping by exploiting the mismatch between the display name and the stored enum value.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `content_source` against `Entry.EntrySource` values before passing it to `delete_all_entries`. For example: `if content_source not in Entry.EntrySource.values: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid content source")`. Also ensure the string passed to `delete_all_entries` matches the actual stored enum value (e.g., `"computer"`, `"notion"`, `"github"`) rather than relying on the raw URL path parameter.

findings.explanation: In `get_all_filenames`, the user-supplied `content_source` path parameter is passed directly to `EntryAdapters.aget_all_filenames_by_source(user, content_source)` without validation against the `EntrySource` enum. While the query is scoped to `user`, an authenticated user can supply any arbitrary string as `content_source`. If they supply a value that does not match any `EntrySource`, the query returns an empty list (harmless), but if they supply a value matching another user's tagged source through a naming collision or future source addition, it reveals which file paths exist for that source. More importantly, no validation ensures `content_source` is one of the declared `EntrySource` choices before it is used in the filter, making the authorization check incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `content_source` against `Entry.EntrySource.values` before calling `aget_all_filenames_by_source`. Raise an HTTP 400 or 422 error if the value is not a recognized source.

### Khoj Chat
#### Overview
- Creates a personal assistant for you to inquire and engage with your notes
- You can choose to use Online or Offline Chat depending on your requirements
- Supports multi-turn conversations with the relevant notes for context
- Shows reference notes used to generate a response

### Setup
#### Offline Chat
Offline chat stays completely private and works without internet. But it is slower, lower quality and more compute intensive.

> **System Requirements**:
>  - Minimum 8 GB RAM. Recommend **16Gb VRAM**
>  - Minimum **5 GB of Disk** available
>  - A CPU supporting [AVX or AVX2 instructions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Vector_Extensions) is required
>  - A Mac M1+ or [Vulcan supported GPU](https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/) should significantly speed up chat response times

Online chat requires internet to use ChatGPT but is faster, higher quality and less compute intensive.

# Setup the Github integration

The Github integration allows you to index as many repositories as you want. It's currently default configured to index Issues, Commits, and all Markdown/Org files in each repository. For large repositories, this takes a fairly long time, but it works well for smaller projects.

3. Click `Save`. Go back to the settings page and click `Configure`.

# Telemetry

We collect some high level, anonymized metadata about usage of Khoj. This includes:
- Client (Web, Emacs, Obsidian)
- API usage (Search, Chat)
- Configured content types (Github, Org, etc)
- Request metadata (e.g., host, referrer)

We don't send any personal information or any information from/about your content. We only send the above metadata. This helps us prioritize feature development and understand how people are using Khoj. Don't just take our word for it -- you can see [the code here](https://github.com/khoj-ai/khoj/tree/master/src/telemetry).

## Disable Telemetry

You can opt out of telemetry at any time. To do so,
1. Open `~/.khoj/khoj.yml`
2. Set `should-log-telemetry` to `false`
3. Save the file and restart Khoj

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/BDgyabRM6e).
